question: Can all objects of this kind be organized into a complete description?
idea: A classification aims to describe every object satisfying specified conditions, rather than just produce a few examples. The assumptions define which objects belong in the collection. This entry states a particular classification claim.
why: The study of shapes defined by equations, often using complex numbers. It connects geometric features with algebraic rules.

glossary.meaning: A geometric setting that includes points at infinity, making many geometric relationships more uniform.
A kind of geometric space in which complex coordinates, lengths, and an additional geometric structure are compatible.
A space that looks like ordinary flat space when you examine a sufficiently small neighborhood.
A mathematical condition that rules out certain forms of escaping to infinity; in ordinary Euclidean space it means closed and bounded.
A mathematical statement proposed to be true but requiring proof or a counterexample.
A description of all objects of a specified kind, usually organized into recognizable types.
A way of measuring the number of independent directions or degrees of freedom; different theories use different notions.

exactClaim: Proves the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture: every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kähler manifold of real dimension at least eight is homothetic to a compact symmetric Wolf space. It also proves contact-Fano homogeneity and classifies smooth connected complex projective contact manifolds of complex dimension at least three: those with $b_2=1$ are adjoint varieties with their canonical contact structures, while those with $b_2\ge2$ have underlying manifold $\mathbb P(T^*Z)$ for a smooth projective variety Z.
scope: A definition-led reading guide; the exact mathematical claim is preserved separately. This is not a proof assessment.
